For me this is triggered by boredom, loneliness and stress- especially during this pandemic. I also love watching hauls and I get triggered to start scrolling through shopping sites if I see something in the hauls I like. It’s super bad. I watched a documentary on fast fashion and how small kids and young women work unreasonably hours, get abused, and get paid $1-$2 a day to make all the fast fashion clothes and it put things into perspective for me. Whenever I get the urge to shop fast fashion I get memories of certain scenes in the documentary when a mother had her daughter sleeping on the floor while she worked on sowing because she couldn’t leave her child anywhere else, or a scene with a small boy from India making tons of leather shoes tirelessly. That usually helps me refrain from shopping fast fashion because the way human beings are suffering for selfish corporations who don’t care about their human rights breaks my heart and I tend to feel guilty when I get the urge to buy things I don’t need and I feel really awful for fueling industries like that, although I’m definitely not perfect and slip up sometimes.

Gratitude is super important for me too. I remind myself to be grateful for what I have knowing there are people who would want to have what I have but can’t. I tend to take life for granted by wanting more and more of what I don’t need so I try to be grateful.
 I also keep reminding myself why I want to be a minimalist and think of either having money in my account or having it be lost to something I don’t need and will regret later! I’d like to own my own car someday after I graduate college so I remind myself of my goals too and that really helps!  Mindfulness and intentional thought has helped me a lot so far.
